topology: VLAN 10 has DHCP PCs on SW1 Gi0/1–2, gateway/DHCP router R1 192.168.10.1 on Gi0/3, static SRV2 192.168.10.50 (0200.0010.0050) on Gi0/4 and ARP test host PC3 192.168.10.60 on Gi0/5. R1 Gi0/1 192.168.20.1 routes to remote HTTP/DNS server SRV1 192.168.20.10. Addresses, access VLANs, PortFast, router DHCP and server services are prepared.
verificationNotes: Practice begins unprotected at zero earned tasks even after existing legitimate DHCP leases. Applying the published IOS reference earns five policy tasks; admitted DHCP ACKs earn two dynamic-binding tasks. Real routed pings, static ARP acceptance, a forged-claim drop and the current correct gateway neighbor complete all twelve.

DHCP snooping is enabled globally and for VLAN 10 with Option 82 insertion disabled for this router-served pool. Only Gi0/3 has DHCP server trust. ARP inspection and src-mac/dst-mac/IP validation protect VLAN 10; separate ARP trust is exclusive to Gi0/3. All four attached untrusted access ports have explicit 15pps ARP limits.

The exact static-server IP/MAC ACL is applied without static; unmatched clients fall back to DHCP snooping bindings. A static filter, a wrong static MAC, a missing ACL and broad permits are tested. Broad permit-any cannot satisfy the exact-host policy or static-acceptance observation.

Guide ARP tests use the existing real frame path to emit gratuitous ARP, not fictional Windows CLI syntax. PC3 keeps its actual .60 address while falsely claiming .1 with its own NIC MAC. A correlated received ingress/drop packet proves rejection; counters or unrelated drops cannot award credit. Static acceptance requires exact ACL rule evidence, delivery to PC1 and the real learned MAC.

Trusting the test-host ingress or disabling VLAN inspection admits the same forged claim and poisons endpoint gateway caches. Restoring inspection does not rewrite caches. arp -d * on both clients followed by fresh routed pings repairs them. Removing gateway ARP trust blocks real gateway replies even while DHCP trust is retained.

Clearing snooping bindings leaves cached paths temporarily usable; clear endpoint caches to expose the missing-binding failure, then renew to rebuild dynamic entries. Explicit ARP rate violations err-disable the offending port and recover through corrected limits plus shutdown/no shutdown.

Configuration, actual blocked/accepted ARP achievements and valid ping observations survive portable saves. Dynamic DHCP binding and live gateway-cache tasks rebuild from traffic after reopening. The completed reference includes no fabricated runtime evidence.

ARP ingress decisions retain bounded 1000-row telemetry and rejected ARP trace entries include actual packet identity and addresses. Existing policy algorithms and CLI styling are preserved. Inspection statistics expose aggregate drops; per-VLAN/per-cause counters are not advertised as implemented.
